name: Sea of Cloud
desc: Standing above the inversion looking out over an undercast — five strata of billowing cloud run to the horizon, the near ones huge and sliding fast, the far ones small and almost still, with dark ridges breaching the deck between them so cloud passes in front of some peaks and behind others, and the whole sea breathes up and down over minutes; a cold alpine inversion, sunrise alpenglow, moonlit silver, a topographic sheet of the cloud surface, or a water-vapour satellite channel.

energy.doc: how hard the light burns — the sun's bloom through the deck, wisp brightness and overall contrast

scale.doc: billow size and ridge height — big scale gives a coarse, monumental deck (rebuilds every stratum)

density.doc: how tightly packed the billows are, and how many wisps tear off the deck

speed.doc: how fast the deck slides — near strata always move faster than far ones

billow.doc: convection — from a flat oily deck to a boiling cauliflower sea

peaks.doc: how far the ridges breach the cloud — 0 drowns them entirely, 1 stands them clear

hue.doc: palette hue shift off the default cold blue-white

x.doc: where the sun stands — the billow crowns light from that side

y.doc: the horizon — how much frame is sky versus cloud sea

style.doc: aesthetic: inversion = deep zenith over a cold white deck, blue-black peaks, large-format; alpenglow = sunrise, the cloud sea takes the fire and the peaks stay cold; moonlit = silver deck, dark key; topo = the cloud surface as a topographic sheet, stacked contours, no mass and no light; watervapour = a meteorological satellite channel where form is built from brightness temperature rather than light

act.doc: multi-minute programme — the deck settling, rising to drown the peaks, or burning off beneath you

seed.doc: regenerates the billow field, the ridges and the wisps

alpha.doc: how far the world sits back behind the performers
